messages:
Amy: quick q — for the precision profiles RFC follow-up, are we leaning toward allowing user-level per-route precision overrides, or should we keep it server-side only for now?
Devon: leaning server-side + profiles exposed as named presets. user overrides are a big surface for safety/regression risk.
Sasha: we ran a short eval yesterday — allowing arbitrary per-route overrides caused ~3% tail-regression on our chat eval set when combined with kv-cache reuse. not catastrophic but noisy.
Amy: ok that matches my worry. what about a guarded override where users can request a profile but the control plane validates against eval thresholds?
Devon: yeah — something like: allow override but require a signed "compat report" from the customer's eval harness or force it into canary rollout with metric gates.
Pranay: +1. metric gates we care about: per-token loss delta, answer-coherence score, hallucination rate (we use our checker), and 99th pct latency.
Lee: important: the runtime must be able to attach a "profile metadata" to cached kv entries so different precision variants don't corrupt each other's cache. that means serializing precision version into cache keys.
Sasha: note: for int8->fp8 mix we saw small numeric drift after cache reheating. workaround: versioned cache keys + conservative TTL for mixed-precision warmups.
Devon: concrete API proposal: expose POST /profiles (managed by infra) returning profile-id. Client can reference profile-id in requests. No raw precision fields accepted unless tenant has "advanced-precision" flag.
Amy: can we sketch the profile json?
Devon: sure — example:
```
{
  "id":"latency-4bit-v1",
  "primary_precision":"int4",
  "fallback_chain":["int8","fp16"],
  "layer_overrides":[{"pattern":"attn_*","precision":"fp8"}],
  "safety_thresholds":{"loss_delta":0.02,"hallucination_delta":0.01}
}
```
Pranay: love it. two questions: 1) how do we compute hallucination_delta automatically? 2) who enforces the safety_thresholds?
Sasha: hallucination checks come from running our eval prompts + classifier; we emit a fingerprint. Control plane enforces thresholds at rollout time (canary evaluation) and runtime via sampled background evals.
Lee: enforcement at runtime: if a sampled request fails safety checks we increment a per-profile error counter and can trigger instantaneous rollback for the profile via policy. needs hook into the rollout/rt-config service.
Devon: rollout policy options: immediate rollback if X failures in Y minutes, or gradual ramp with automatic backoff. default: 5 failures / 10k samples triggers rollback.
Amy: what's the strategy for quantization calibration slots? e.g., we need holdout buckets to ensure calibration data isn't leaked into live inference.
Sasha: we separate calibration traffic. the build (quantizer) runs on held-out corpora and generates calibration tables/artifacts attached to profile. runtime refuses to accept runtime-calibrated artifacts unless explicitly marked experimental.
Pranay: ops question — storage/versioning for quant artifacts: prefer similar pattern to model bundles (immutable URI + checksum). also require KMS-signed artifact manifests for private deployments.
Lee: runtime compatibility: we need a deterministic kernel selection layer. different kernels for int8 vs fp8 -> choose by (profile_id, seq_len, batch_size) mapping at request time. fallback chain must be cheap to evaluate.
Devon: good call. Also add a "quality_guard" boolean on profile to block use in production routes unless manually approved by SRE/product.
Amy: evaluation infra: for any profile PR we should auto-run: (1) unit evals, (2) canary on 0.5% traffic for 6 hours with shadow comparison, (3) full rollout if no regressions.
Sasha: add regression thresholds for embeddings (cosine drop) and for generations (BLEU/ROUGE/F1 depending on task). default thresholds live in a config store.
Pranay: logging/telemetry: per-request attach profile_id, precision_used, kernel_id, cache_hit, quant_artifact_checksum. make these high-card but sampled.
Lee: also emit a "precision_mismatch" metric when cache key precision != current precision to detect stale entries.
Devon: security: private deployments need to be able to pin allowed profiles via config. prevent remote profile fetch for air-gapped.
Amy: OK. Can someone write a short RFC addendum summarizing: API shape, lifecycle (build->canary->rollout->rollback), runtime changes (cache versioning, kernel mapping), telemetry keys, and enforcement rules?
Sasha: i'll draft it today and ping for review. will include perf numbers from the int4 experiments.
Pranay: i'll add the artifact signing + KMS section.
Devon: I'll handle the control-plane enforcement bits and the rollout defaults.
Amy: perfect. thanks — let's aim to merge before next eng-ml sync. :thumbsup:
